title: Bernard diary: geographic identifications for map
method: Diary evidence and external geographical identification are kept separate. All pins are approximate locality points, not reconstructed 1941 ship, station, camp or personal positions. Uncertain readings stay uncertain. Addresses, drawings and external unit histories do not prove visits.
coordinateSystem: WGS84 decimal degrees; pin fields lat/lon
coordinateAuthority: NGA Geographic Names Server, queried 2026-10-10; raw responses in work/geography-nga-uppercase-queries.json. Rounded displayed pins intentionally reduce false precision.

places.diaryEvidence: Arrived Port Tewfic 3 May 1941; anchored at Suez until disembarkation on 6 May; separate tentative departure note 4 August; labelled sketch.
places.evidenceStatus: recorded arrival and disembarkation; later departure is tentative
places.identification: Port Tewfik / Port Tawfiq (Bur Tawfiq), at Suez and the southern Suez Canal entrance

pin.label: Port Tewfic / Suez — port vicinity
pin.accuracy: rounded settlement vicinity; not the ship anchorage, berth or 1941 landing point

places.diaryEvidence: Arrived at El Kantara about 4 pm on 6 May; receiving depot overnight; train departure 5:30 am 7 May 1941 for Gaza.
places.identification: Al Qantarah on the Suez Canal; the text explicitly mentions Kantara East
places.identificationConfidence: high for locality; exact depot and rail platform unresolved

pin.label: Kantara — town and canal vicinity
pin.accuracy: rounded locality point; not the receiving depot, landing or Kantara East station

places.diaryEvidence: Passed through Romani and El Erich by train on 7 May 1941.

sources.title: Australian Light Horse—Palestine 1916–1918
sources.supportingText: The official history account connects Romani, Kantara and El Arish with the Sinai campaign and railway advance.

sources.title: Geographic Names Server: Romani

The nearby salt-flat record is a different feature and is not a substitute station coordinate.

places.diaryEvidence: Arrived 7 May and left 17 May 1941; movement onward to Julis.
places.identificationConfidence: high for named camp and broad region

sources.supportingText: Kilo 89 Camp, Gaza Ridge, Palestine. c. December 1941.

sources.title: Kilo 89 camp, Gaza, Palestine, 1942 (P02480.009)
sources.supportingText: Kilo 89 camp, Gaza, Palestine. 1942.

cautions: No precise camp position established. Gaza city coordinates must not be labelled as Kilo 89 camp.
An AWM graves-unit index labels Kilo 89 as Egypt; contemporaneous photo catalogues and diary route support the Palestine camp. The conflicting index is not a basis for moving the pin to Egypt.

places.diaryEvidence: Arrived unit Julis, [Gellibrand?] lines on 17 May 1941; repeated as JOIN 3RD BTN AT JULIUS.
places.evidenceStatus: recorded arrival at named camp; line-name transcription tentative
places.identification: Southern Palestine Julis camp near Gaza, with Gellibrand one of its documented sections; locality corresponds to abandoned Julis/Julius rather than Galilee Julis
places.identificationConfidence: high for camp identity; exact Gellibrand Lines location unresolved

pin.label: Julis — approximate historical locality
pin.accuracy: rounded NGA abandoned-settlement point, used only for the surrounding locality; camp perimeter and Gellibrand Lines are unlocated

sources.title: To Benghazi, chapter 4
sources.supportingText: The five sections at Julis were named Monash, Goddard, Gellibrand, Hobbs and Leane.

sources.title: Main Tel Aviv–Gaza road through Julis Camp (023609)
sources.supportingText: The catalogue identifies the main Tel Aviv–Gaza road through Julis Camp, with the view towards Gaza.

sources.title: 2/1st Australian Infantry Battalion
sources.supportingText: Unit history locates the 16th Brigade concentration at Julis near Gaza.

cautions: Gellibrand remains bracketed in the transcription; external corroboration belongs in the map annotation.

Pin represents historical locality, not the exact Australian camp or lines.

sources.title: Rehovoth cancelled postage stamps, 1939–1940

The revised initials [7 AGH?] remain tentative. AWM photograph 022693 places the 7th Australian General Hospital near Rehovot, but this does not establish Bernard’s admission or the reason for his journey.
places.reviewNote: Handwriting rechecked 10 October 2026; [A S A?] replaced with tentative [7 AGH?]. Historical hospital context: https://www.awm.gov.au/collection/C6754.
